name: Khozema Shipchandler
current_role: CEO and board member, Twilio Inc.; director, Ethos Technologies
profile: Twilio's CEO since January 2024, succeeding co-founder Jeff Lawson. He joined Twilio as CFO in 2018, then served as COO and President of Twilio Communications. Before Twilio he spent over two decades at GE in finance and operating roles across Industrial Internet (GE Digital), Corporate Audit and Aviation.
interesting_fact: He rose from CFO (2018) to COO (2021) to President of Twilio Communications (2023) and then CEO (Jan 2024), one of the few finance chiefs to take over from a founder-CEO at a major developer-platform company.
deep_cut_fact: His GE career took him abroad: he held operating and financial roles at GE in the U.S., the Middle East and Singapore, across Industrial Internet, Corporate Audit and Aviation. He is an Indiana University Bloomington graduate.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Twilio press office. Speaks at Twilio SIGNAL conferences.

name: Illiya I. Pesic
current_role: Director (and 10%+ shareholder), Silvaco Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: SVCO)
profile: Iliya Pesic is the son of Ivan Pesic, who founded TCAD/EDA software maker Silvaco in 1984; the family remains a major shareholder. Iliya joined Silvaco's board in 2012, served as Chair (2012-14) and Executive Chair (2014-21), stepped off the board in 2023 and rejoined it in May 2025, after Silvaco's 2024 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: Silvaco makes TCAD (technology computer-aided design) software used to simulate semiconductor processes and devices, an unusual niche of chip-design tooling; Pesic led the board as Executive Chair for seven years before the company went public.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.S. in electronic engineering from Tohoku University in Sendai, Japan (after a B.S. EE from Santa Clara University), and before chairing Silvaco worked as a senior process engineer in a fabrication facility in the MEMS and biomedical industries.
notes: Spelled 'Iliya' in company materials (SEC lists 'Illiya'). Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Route via Silvaco IR/press.

name: Troy Rudd
current_role: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, AECOM (NYSE: ACM)
profile: Troy Rudd has led global infrastructure consultancy AECOM as CEO since August 2020 (now also Chairman), refocusing it on professional services, advisory and program management in water, energy, transportation and buildings. He joined AECOM in 2009 and was previously its CFO; before that he was a KPMG partner for 10 years.
interesting_fact: AECOM credits his tenure with a near tripling of its market capitalization since he became CEO; the firm posted $16.1B of revenue in fiscal 2025 and works on energy and data-center-adjacent infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: A tax specialist by training, he holds a Master of Science in Taxation from Golden Gate University and a B.S. from the University of British Columbia; he sits on the Executive Board of SMU's Lyle School of Engineering and on the Sustainable Markets Initiative board.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center infrastructure topics. Press contact is AECOM's head of global communications as listed on 2025 releases; confirm current before use.

name: Ellen R Patterson
current_role: Senior EVP and General Counsel, Wells Fargo & Company; member of the Operating Committee
profile: Ellen Patterson has been Wells Fargo's General Counsel since March 2020, leading global legal affairs, litigation and regulatory matters and advising on corporate governance during the bank's long regulatory remediation. She was previously Group Head and General Counsel of TD Bank Group and, before that, a Simpson Thacher & Bartlett partner focused on M&A for financial institutions.
interesting_fact: American Banker profiled her as a 'Most Powerful Woman to Watch' for her role in steering Wells Fargo's legal and regulatory clean-up after the fake-accounts era.
deep_cut_fact: A Harvard College and Columbia Law School (1998) graduate, she spent about 14 years at Simpson Thacher before moving to Toronto-based TD; at Wells Fargo she is co-executive sponsor of the Women's Connection employee network.
notes: Bank GC, not an entrepreneur; low media profile and limited fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Route via Wells Fargo corporate communications (newsroom media contacts page).
